# `device` reference

Every method of the `device` global, with its arguments, return value,
errors, where it works, and an example. The
[Device API guide](https://ganymede-server.com/docs/ganymede-ui/device)
explains where `device` exists and how to call it from a server kernel
or a browser.

`device` is `undefined` on kernels the app doesn't host, so a cell
checks for it first (`device?.clipboard.readText()`, or
`if (device) …`). The examples skip that check, and the
[`SoundPlayer`](#soundplayer) examples use a `player` from
[`device.sound.player`](#device-sound-player-data-options).

For editor types, add this line once to a cell or a project file:

```ts
/// <reference types="@tlockney/ganymede-device/globals" />
```

Every method takes a last `options` argument with a `signal`
([`CallOptions`](#calloptions)), and fails with a
[`DeviceError`](#errors). **Availability** says where each method
works: in the app (a kernel the Mac, iPad or iPhone app runs itself),
the system permission it needs there, from a [remote
kernel](https://ganymede-server.com/docs/ganymede-ui/device#from-a-server-kernel)
in the app, and from a kernel driven from a
[browser](https://ganymede-server.com/docs/ganymede-ui/device#in-a-browser).
"planned" means it doesn't yet but will; "no" means the platform has no
such API.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`device.info(options?)`](#device-info-options) | Reads what the host is and the device's current state. |
| [`device.has(method)`](#device-has-method) | Whether the host answers a method. |
| [`device.openURL(url, options?)`](#device-openurl-url-options) | Opens a link: in the browser, or the mail app for `mailto`. |
| [`device.share(options)`](#device-share-options) | Shows the system share sheet (`NSSharingServicePicker` on the Mac). |
| [`device.preview(files, options?)`](#device-preview-files-options) | Shows files in Quick Look. |
| [`device.clipboard.readText(options?)`](#device-clipboard-readtext-options) | Reads the clipboard's text. |
| [`device.clipboard.writeText(text, options?)`](#device-clipboard-writetext-text-options) | Replaces the clipboard's contents with `text`. |
| [`device.clipboard.readImage(options?)`](#device-clipboard-readimage-options) | Reads the clipboard's image as PNG bytes, whatever format was copied. |
| [`device.clipboard.writeImage(image, options?)`](#device-clipboard-writeimage-image-options) | Replaces the clipboard's contents with an image. |
| [`device.haptics.impact(style?, options?)`](#device-haptics-impact-style-options) | Plays a tap. |
| [`device.haptics.notification(type, options?)`](#device-haptics-notification-type-options) | Plays the system's success, warning or error pattern. |
| [`device.haptics.selection(options?)`](#device-haptics-selection-options) | Plays the tick of a picker moving to a new value. |
| [`device.ui.alert(message, options?)`](#device-ui-alert-message-options) | Shows a message with an OK button. |
| [`device.ui.confirm(message, options?)`](#device-ui-confirm-message-options) | Asks a yes-or-no question. |
| [`device.ui.prompt(message, options?)`](#device-ui-prompt-message-options) | Asks for a line of text. |
| [`device.ui.actionSheet(title, options, sheetOptions?)`](#device-ui-actionsheet-title-options-sheetoptions) | Asks the person to choose one of several options. |
| [`device.ui.pickDate(options?)`](#device-ui-pickdate-options) | Asks for a date, a time, or both. |
| [`device.files.pick(options?)`](#device-files-pick-options) | Shows the open panel on the Mac, or the document picker on iPad and iPhone, and reads the files the person picks. |
| [`device.files.export(data, options)`](#device-files-export-data-options) | Asks where to save `data`, and saves it there: the save panel on the Mac, the document picker on iPad and iPhone. |
| [`device.photos.pick(options?)`](#device-photos-pick-options) | Shows the system photo picker and reads the photos the person picks. |
| [`device.sound.play(data, options?)`](#device-sound-play-data-options) | Starts playing a sound, which plays to its end on its own. |
| [`device.sound.player(data, options?)`](#device-sound-player-data-options) | Loads a sound into a player, paused at the start, for a cell to play, pause, seek and close. |
| [`device.notifications.authorizationStatus(options?)`](#device-notifications-authorizationstatus-options) | Reads the permission's status, without asking. |
| [`device.notifications.isAuthorized(options?)`](#device-notifications-isauthorized-options) | Whether the permission is granted, without asking. |
| [`device.notifications.requestAuthorization(options?)`](#device-notifications-requestauthorization-options) | Shows the system prompt when the person hasn't been asked, and resolves with the status after it; otherwise resolves with the status as it is. |
| [`device.notifications.schedule(body, options)`](#device-notifications-schedule-body-options) | Schedules a notification to show after a delay, even if the notebook or the app has closed by then. |
| [`device.notifications.pending(options?)`](#device-notifications-pending-options) | Lists this notebook's notifications that haven't been delivered yet. |
| [`device.notifications.cancel(id, options?)`](#device-notifications-cancel-id-options) | Takes one of this notebook's notifications off the schedule. |
| [`device.notifications.cancelAll(options?)`](#device-notifications-cancelall-options) | Takes all of this notebook's notifications off the schedule. |
| [`player.play(options?)`](#player-play-options) | Plays from the current time. |
| [`player.pause(options?)`](#player-pause-options) | Pauses at the current time. |
| [`player.stop(options?)`](#player-stop-options) | Pauses and goes back to the start. |
| [`player.seek(seconds, options?)`](#player-seek-seconds-options) | Moves to a time, playing or not. |
| [`player.setVolume(volume, options?)`](#player-setvolume-volume-options) | Sets the volume. |
| [`player.state(options?)`](#player-state-options) | Reads the player's state, changing nothing. |
| [`player.close()`](#player-close) | Stops the player and frees it; later calls fail `failed`. |

## `device`

The `device` global: native features of the Mac, iPad and iPhone apps.
Undefined on kernels the app doesn't host, so check for it first.

### `device.info(options?)`

```ts
info(options?: CallOptions): Promise<DeviceInfo>;
```

Reads what the host is and the device's current state.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<DeviceInfo>`: The host's answer to `hello` as it was when the kernel started, with the current screen, battery, appearance and locale where the host reads them.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | yes |

A browser has no model or battery.

```ts
const info = await device.info();
console.log(info.platform, info.osVersion, info.battery?.level);
```

### `device.has(method)`

```ts
has(method: string): boolean;
```

Whether the host answers a method. Synchronous: it reads what the host
said when the kernel started, so it can't be cancelled.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` | `string` | yes | A method's name as `SUPPORT` lists it, such as `"clipboard.readText"` or `"openURL"`. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `true` when the host answers it; calling a method it doesn't fails `unavailable`.

```ts
if (device.has("haptics.impact")) await device.haptics.impact();
else console.log("no haptics on", (await device.info()).platform);
```

### `device.openURL(url, options?)`

```ts
openURL(url: string | URL, options?: OpenURLOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Opens a link: in the browser, or the mail app for `mailto`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string \| URL` | yes | An `http`, `https` or `mailto` URL. |
| `options` | `OpenURLOptions` | no | `inApp` shows a web page in the app on iPhone and iPad, and the call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the URL may already have opened. |

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` for any other scheme.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

http, https and mailto only. `inApp` works on iPhone and iPad, not the Mac; a browser opens a tab after a click, and ignores `inApp`.

```ts
await device.openURL("https://ganymede-server.com/docs/", { inApp: true });
```

### `device.share(options)`

```ts
share(options: ShareOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Shows the system share sheet (`NSSharingServicePicker` on the Mac).
The sheet is its own consent, so no permission.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `ShareOptions` | yes | `text`, `url` and `files` to share (at least one; files together at most 16 MiB), and the call's `signal`, which closes the sheet and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the person picked where to send them (on iPhone and iPad once the share completes; on the Mac as soon as they pick a service), `false` when they dismissed it.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when there is nothing to share, a file has no plain name, or the files are over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

The share sheet; `NSSharingServicePicker` on the Mac. A browser uses the Web Share API, after a click, and shares files only where it can.

```ts
const csv = "city,temp\nOslo,4\nLima,19\n";
await device.share({
  text: "Today's temperatures",
  files: [{ name: "temps.csv", data: new TextEncoder().encode(csv) }],
});
```

### `device.preview(files, options?)`

```ts
preview(files: NamedBytes[], options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Shows files in Quick Look. Quick Look picks the viewer from each
name's extension, so name a PNG `*.png`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | `NamedBytes[]` | yes | The files, together at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`, which closes Quick Look and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** once the person closes it.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `files` is empty, a file has no plain name, or the files are over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | no |

Quick Look, which picks the viewer from each file name's extension. A browser has no Quick Look.

```ts
const png = await device.clipboard.readImage();
if (png) await device.preview([{ name: "clipboard.png", data: png }]);
```

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clipboard` | `Clipboard` | The system clipboard: see `Clipboard`. |
| `haptics` | `Haptics` | Taptic feedback, on iPhone: see `Haptics`. |
| `ui` | `UI` | Dialogs over the notebook: see `UI`. |
| `files` | `Files` | The system's file pickers: see `Files`. |
| `photos` | `Photos` | The system photo picker: see `Photos`. |
| `sound` | `Sound` | Sound playback: see `Sound`. |
| `notifications` | `Notifications` | Local notifications after a delay: see `Notifications`. |

## `device.clipboard`

The system clipboard. iPadOS may show its paste prompt on a read.

### `device.clipboard.readText(options?)`

```ts
readText(options?: CallOptions): Promise<string | null>;
```

Reads the clipboard's text.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<string | null>`: The text, or `null` when the clipboard holds none.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

iPadOS shows its paste prompt; a browser needs a click for the Clipboard API.

```ts
const text = await device.clipboard.readText();
if (text !== null) console.log(text.split(/\s+/).length, "words");
```

### `device.clipboard.writeText(text, options?)`

```ts
writeText(text: string, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Replaces the clipboard's contents with `text`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | yes | The text to copy. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the write may already have happened. |

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

A browser needs a click for the Clipboard API.

```ts
await device.clipboard.writeText(JSON.stringify({ rows: 3 }, null, 2));
```

### `device.clipboard.readImage(options?)`

```ts
readImage(options?: CallOptions): Promise<Uint8Array | null>;
```

Reads the clipboard's image as PNG bytes, whatever format was copied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<Uint8Array | null>`: PNG bytes, or `null` when the clipboard holds no image.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

PNG. iPadOS shows its paste prompt; a browser needs a click for the Clipboard API.

```ts
const png = await device.clipboard.readImage();
if (png) console.log(`${png.byteLength} bytes`);
```

### `device.clipboard.writeImage(image, options?)`

```ts
writeImage(image: Bytes, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Replaces the clipboard's contents with an image.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | `Bytes` | yes | PNG, JPEG, GIF, HEIC or TIFF bytes, at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the write may already have happened. |

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when the bytes aren't an image the device reads.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

A browser needs a click for the Clipboard API, and takes PNG only.

```ts
const [photo] = await device.photos.pick();
if (photo) await device.clipboard.writeImage(photo);
```

## `device.haptics`

Taptic feedback. iPhone only: iPads and Macs have no Taptic Engine, so
there `device.has("haptics.impact")` is false and calls fail
`unavailable`.

### `device.haptics.impact(style?, options?)`

```ts
impact(style?: ImpactStyle, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Plays a tap.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | `ImpactStyle` | no | How strong a tap: `"light"`, `"medium"` (the default), `"heavy"`, `"soft"` or `"rigid"`. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the tap may already have played. |

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone | none | yes | no |

iPhone only: iPads and Macs have no Taptic Engine. A browser has no haptics API Safari supports.

```ts
if (device.has("haptics.impact")) await device.haptics.impact("heavy");
```

### `device.haptics.notification(type, options?)`

```ts
notification(type: NotificationFeedback, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Plays the system's success, warning or error pattern.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `NotificationFeedback` | yes | `"success"`, `"warning"` or `"error"`. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone | none | yes | no |

iPhone only: iPads and Macs have no Taptic Engine.

```ts
await device.haptics.notification("success");
```

### `device.haptics.selection(options?)`

```ts
selection(options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Plays the tick of a picker moving to a new value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone | none | yes | no |

iPhone only: iPads and Macs have no Taptic Engine.

```ts
for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
  await device.haptics.selection();
  await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, 200));
}
```

## `device.ui`

Dialogs the app shows over the notebook: sheets on the Mac, alerts on
iPhone and iPad. One shows at a time; a second call waits for the first
to close. Dismissing one is not an error: it returns `null` or `false`.
An interrupt or an aborted `signal` closes it and rejects `cancelled`
(`timeout` for `AbortSignal.timeout()`).

### `device.ui.alert(message, options?)`

```ts
alert(message: string, options?: AlertOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Shows a message with an OK button.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | yes | The message. |
| `options` | `AlertOptions` | no | `title` is a heading above it; `signal` cancels: it closes the alert and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** once the person closes it.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

A sheet on the Mac, an alert on iPhone and iPad; a browser will show it in the cell's output.

```ts
await device.ui.alert("The import finished: 1,204 rows.", { title: "Done" });
```

### `device.ui.confirm(message, options?)`

```ts
confirm(message: string, options?: ConfirmOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Asks a yes-or-no question.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | yes | The question. |
| `options` | `ConfirmOptions` | no | `title`, `okLabel` for the confirming button, `destructive` to show it red, and the call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the person confirms, `false` when they cancel or dismiss it.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

```ts
if (await device.ui.confirm("Delete the scratch files?", { destructive: true, okLabel: "Delete" })) {
  console.log("deleting");
}
```

### `device.ui.prompt(message, options?)`

```ts
prompt(message: string, options?: PromptOptions): Promise<string | null>;
```

Asks for a line of text.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | yes | The question. |
| `options` | `PromptOptions` | no | `title`, `placeholder`, `defaultValue`, `secure` to hide what is typed, and the call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<string | null>`: The text entered, or `null` when the person cancels.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

```ts
const name = await device.ui.prompt("Name the run", { defaultValue: "baseline" });
if (name !== null) console.log(`saving ${name}`);
```

### `device.ui.actionSheet(title, options, sheetOptions?)`

```ts
actionSheet(title: string, options: string[], sheetOptions?: ActionSheetOptions): Promise<number | null>;
```

Asks the person to choose one of several options.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | yes | The sheet's heading. |
| `options` | `string[]` | yes | The choices' labels, at least one. |
| `sheetOptions` | `ActionSheetOptions` | no | `message` under the title, `cancel` for the cancel button's label, `destructive` for the index of an option to show red, and the call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<number | null>`: The index of the option chosen, or `null` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `options` is empty.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

```ts
const formats = ["CSV", "JSON", "Parquet"];
const i = await device.ui.actionSheet("Export as", formats);
if (i !== null) console.log(`exporting ${formats[i]}`);
```

### `device.ui.pickDate(options?)`

```ts
pickDate(options?: PickDateOptions): Promise<Date | null>;
```

Asks for a date, a time, or both.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `PickDateOptions` | no | `mode` (`"date"`, `"time"` or `"datetime"`, the default), `title`, `value` to start at, `min` and `max`, and the call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<Date | null>`: The date chosen, or `null` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `value`, `min` or `max` isn't a valid `Date`.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | planned |

```ts
const start = await device.ui.pickDate({ mode: "date", title: "Report from", max: new Date() });
if (start) console.log(start.toISOString().slice(0, 10));
```

## `device.files`

Files in and out through the system's own pickers, which are the
person's consent, so no permission. A picked file is copied in by value:
the notebook keeps no access to where it came from.

### `device.files.pick(options?)`

```ts
pick(options?: PickFilesOptions): Promise<File[]>;
```

Shows the open panel on the Mac, or the document picker on iPad and
iPhone, and reads the files the person picks. Together they are at
most 16 MiB.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `PickFilesOptions` | no | `types` limits what can be picked, `multiple` allows more than one, and `signal` cancels: it closes the picker and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<File[]>`: The picked files, with their names and MIME types, or `[]` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `types` or `multiple` has the wrong type, or the files together are over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

The open panel on the Mac, the document picker on iPad and iPhone. Files are copied in; no access to where they came from is kept. A browser can't filter by a type identifier such as `public.json`, so with one it allows any file.

```ts
const [file] = await device.files.pick({ types: [".csv", "text/csv"] });
if (file) {
  const rows = (await file.text()).trim().split("\n");
  console.log(file.name, rows.length, "rows");
}
```

### `device.files.export(data, options)`

```ts
export(data: Bytes, options: ExportFileOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Asks where to save `data`, and saves it there: the save panel on the
Mac, the document picker on iPad and iPhone.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Bytes` | yes | The file's contents, at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `ExportFileOptions` | yes | `name` is the file name the panel suggests; `signal` cancels: it closes the panel and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when saved, `false` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `name` isn't a plain file name, or `data` is over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

The save panel on the Mac, the document picker on iPad and iPhone. A browser downloads it after a click, and answers `true` then, since it can't tell whether it was saved.

```ts
const csv = "city,temp\nOslo,4\nLima,19\n";
const saved = await device.files.export(new TextEncoder().encode(csv), { name: "temps.csv" });
console.log(saved ? "saved" : "cancelled");
```

## `device.photos`

The photo library, through the system photo picker.

### `device.photos.pick(options?)`

```ts
pick(options?: PickPhotosOptions): Promise<File[]>;
```

Shows the system photo picker and reads the photos the person picks.
The picker shows the library without the app being let in, so no
permission. Together the photos are at most 16 MiB.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `PickPhotosOptions` | no | `limit` is how many may be picked (1 by default, 0 for no limit); `signal` cancels: it closes the picker and rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<File[]>`: The picked photos as image `File`s in their stored format (often HEIC or JPEG), or `[]` when the person cancels.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `limit` isn't a whole number of 0 or more, or the photos together are over 16 MiB.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

The system photo picker, which needs no photo library permission. A browser shows a file picker for images, and keeps the first `limit` picked.

```ts
const photos = await device.photos.pick({ limit: 3 });
for (const photo of photos) console.log(photo.name, photo.type, photo.size);
```

## `device.sound`

Sound from bytes in any format the device reads (WAV, AIFF, MP3,
AAC/M4A, CAF, FLAC), at most 16 MiB. No permission. On iPhone the
ring/silent switch can silence it.

### `device.sound.play(data, options?)`

```ts
play(data: Bytes, options?: PlaySoundOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Starts playing a sound, which plays to its end on its own.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Bytes` | yes | The sound's bytes, at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `PlaySoundOptions` | no | `volume` from 0 to 1 (1 by default), and the call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; the sound may already be playing. |

**Returns** once the sound has started.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `data` is empty, over 16 MiB, or not a sound the device reads.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | yes | after a click |

A browser asks for a click only until the page has had one.

```ts
const [file] = await device.files.pick({ types: ["audio/*"] });
if (file) await device.sound.play(file, { volume: 0.5 });
```

### `device.sound.player(data, options?)`

```ts
player(data: Bytes, options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundPlayer>;
```

Loads a sound into a player, paused at the start, for a cell to play,
pause, seek and close. A kernel has at most 32 open at once.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `Bytes` | yes | The sound's bytes, at most 16 MiB. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundPlayer>`: A `SoundPlayer`.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `data` is empty, over 16 MiB, or not a sound the device reads, or the kernel has 32 players open.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

Play, pause, stop, seek and volume; close it, or hold it with `await using`. Remote kernels and browsers: a handle wouldn't survive a disconnect.

```ts
const [file] = await device.files.pick({ types: ["audio/*"] });
if (file) {
  await using player = await device.sound.player(file);
  await player.play();
  // Leaving the block closes the player, which stops it: wait for the end.
  await new Promise((done) => setTimeout(done, player.duration * 1000));
}
```

## `device.notifications`

Local notifications after a delay: the app posts them even when the
notebook or the app is closed. Delay only, no calendar times or
repeats. Each notification belongs to the notebook that scheduled it:
`pending()`, `cancel()` and `cancelAll()` see only that notebook's.

Needs the notifications permission, for `schedule()`: the first call
asks (the app's prompt for this notebook, then the system's) and a
refusal rejects `denied`. `authorizationStatus()`, `isAuthorized()` and
`requestAuthorization()` read and ask for it.

The permission methods (`authorizationStatus`, `isAuthorized`, `requestAuthorization`) work where the rest of the namespace does: in the app, not from a remote kernel or a browser.

### `device.notifications.authorizationStatus(options?)`

```ts
authorizationStatus(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Reads the permission's status, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: `"notDetermined"` until the person is asked, then a grant (`"authorized"`, or a partial one) or `"denied"` or `"restricted"`.

```ts
console.log(await device.notifications.authorizationStatus());
```

### `device.notifications.isAuthorized(options?)`

```ts
isAuthorized(options?: CallOptions): Promise<boolean>;
```

Whether the permission is granted, without asking.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<boolean>`: `true` when the status is a grant, partial ones included.

```ts
if (!(await device.notifications.isAuthorized())) console.log("notifications are off");
```

### `device.notifications.requestAuthorization(options?)`

```ts
requestAuthorization(options?: CallOptions): Promise<AuthorizationStatus>;
```

Shows the system prompt when the person hasn't been asked, and
resolves with the status after it; otherwise resolves with the status
as it is. The namespace's methods ask on their own, so calling this
first is optional. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; a system prompt already
up stays, and its answer still counts for later calls.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<AuthorizationStatus>`: The status after the prompt, or as it was when the person had already been asked.

```ts
const status = await device.notifications.requestAuthorization();
if (status === "denied") console.log("turn notifications on in Settings");
```

### `device.notifications.schedule(body, options)`

```ts
schedule(body: string, options: ScheduleNotificationOptions): Promise<string>;
```

Schedules a notification to show after a delay, even if the notebook
or the app has closed by then. iOS and iPadOS keep at most 64 per
app, dropping the soonest beyond that.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | `string` | yes | The text it shows. |
| `options` | `ScheduleNotificationOptions` | yes | `delay` in seconds (more than 0), an optional `title`, and the call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`; it may already be scheduled. |

**Returns** `Promise<string>`: Its id, for `cancel()`.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `denied` when the notifications permission is refused; `failed` when `body` is empty or `delay` isn't more than 0.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | notifications | no | no |

After `delay` seconds, even when the notebook is closed. iOS and iPadOS keep at most 64 per app.

```ts
const id = await device.notifications.schedule("The training run should be done.", {
  title: "Check the notebook",
  delay: 30 * 60,
});
```

### `device.notifications.pending(options?)`

```ts
pending(options?: CallOptions): Promise<PendingNotification[]>;
```

Lists this notebook's notifications that haven't been delivered yet.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. Cancel rejects `cancelled`. |

**Returns** `Promise<PendingNotification[]>`: This notebook's pending notifications; other notebooks' aren't listed.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

Only the calling notebook's.

```ts
for (const n of await device.notifications.pending()) {
  console.log(n.id, n.body, n.date?.toLocaleTimeString());
}
```

### `device.notifications.cancel(id, options?)`

```ts
cancel(id: string, options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Takes one of this notebook's notifications off the schedule. An id
that's gone, or another notebook's, changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | What `schedule()` returned. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `id` is empty.

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

Only the calling notebook's.

```ts
const id = await device.notifications.schedule("Stretch", { delay: 3600 });
await device.notifications.cancel(id);
```

### `device.notifications.cancelAll(options?)`

```ts
cancelAll(options?: CallOptions): Promise<void>;
```

Takes all of this notebook's notifications off the schedule.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Availability**

| In the app | Permission | Remote kernel | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| yes | none | no | no |

Only the calling notebook's.

```ts
await device.notifications.cancelAll();
```

## `SoundPlayer`

A loaded sound a cell controls, from `device.sound.player`. Close it when
done, or hold it with `await using`. The app closes a kernel's players
when that kernel restarts or shuts down; a kernel has at most 32 open.
Each method answers the player's state after the change.

Its methods work wherever [`device.sound.player`](#device-sound-player-data-options) does.

### `player.play(options?)`

```ts
play(options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Plays from the current time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when the sound can't start, or the player is closed.

```ts
const state = await player.play();
console.log(state.playing, state.duration);
```

### `player.pause(options?)`

```ts
pause(options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Pauses at the current time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

```ts
const { time } = await player.pause();
console.log(`paused at ${time.toFixed(1)} s`);
```

### `player.stop(options?)`

```ts
stop(options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Pauses and goes back to the start.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

```ts
await player.stop();
```

### `player.seek(seconds, options?)`

```ts
seek(seconds: number, options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Moves to a time, playing or not.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seconds` | `number` | yes | The time to move to, in seconds from the start: 0 or more. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `seconds` is negative or not a number.

```ts
await player.seek(player.duration / 2);
await player.play();
```

### `player.setVolume(volume, options?)`

```ts
setVolume(volume: number, options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Sets the volume.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `volume` | `number` | yes | From 0 to 1. |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: The player's state after the change.

**Throws** `DeviceError`: `failed` when `volume` is outside 0 to 1.

```ts
await player.setVolume(0.25);
```

### `player.state(options?)`

```ts
state(options?: CallOptions): Promise<SoundState>;
```

Reads the player's state, changing nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `CallOptions` | no | The call's `signal`. |

**Returns** `Promise<SoundState>`: Whether it is playing, its time and its length.

```ts
const { playing, time } = await player.state();
```

### `player.close()`

```ts
close(): Promise<void>;
```

Stops the player and frees it; later calls fail `failed`. Closing
twice is fine. Leaving an `await using` block closes it too.

```ts
await player.close();
```

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `duration` | `number` | The sound's length in seconds. |

## Errors

A call that fails rejects with a `DeviceError`, an `Error` whose `code` says why. A person dismissing a picker or dialog is not an error.

| `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `unavailable` | No native host, or this platform doesn't have the feature. |
| `denied` | The person or the system refused permission. |
| `cancelled` | Interrupted or aborted before the host answered. |
| `timeout` | The call's `signal` came from `AbortSignal.timeout()` and timed out. |
| `failed` | Anything else, such as an argument the method refuses; the message says what. |
| `disconnected` | The peer went away mid-call, such as a Bluetooth device or a remote link. |

## Types

### `CallOptions`

Every method takes these. Aborting `signal`, or interrupting the kernel,
cancels the call: it rejects with a `DeviceError` whose code is
`cancelled` (`timeout` for `AbortSignal.timeout()`), and the host drops
any dialog or prompt it showed for it.

Where each method works is in `SUPPORT` (src/support.ts); the docs'
table and the reference's Availability lines are generated from it.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` | no | Cancels the call when aborted. In a cdp-kernel cell, `jupyter.signal` aborts when the cell is interrupted. |

### `DeviceInfo`

What the host answers to `hello`, once, before the first cell, and the current state when it answers `info`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `platform` | `string` | yes | `"macos"`, `"ipados"`, `"ios"` or `"browser"`. |
| `appVersion` | `string` | yes | The app's version, such as `"0.5.0"`. |
| `model` | `string` | no | The hardware model identifier, such as `"Mac14,2"` or `"iPad13,4"`. |
| `osVersion` | `string` | no | The operating system's version, such as `"26.1.0"`. |
| `capabilities` | `string[]` | yes | The methods this host answers, such as `"clipboard.readText"`. |
| `isPad` | `boolean` | no | True on an iPad. This and the properties after it are read when `info()` is called, on hosts that answer it. |
| `screen` | `{ width: number; height: number; scale: number }` | no | The main screen in points, and its points-to-pixels scale. |
| `battery` | `{ level: number \| null; charging: boolean }` | no | Absent on a device without a battery. `level` is 0 to 1, or null when unknown. |
| `darkMode` | `boolean` | no | Whether the system appearance is dark. |
| `locale` | `string` | no | The person's locale as a BCP 47 tag, such as `"en-US"`. |

### `OpenURLOptions`

Options for `device.openURL`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `inApp` | `boolean` | no | On iPhone and iPad, show a web page in the app (Safari view) instead of switching to Safari. Ignored on the Mac. |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `ImpactStyle`

The strength of a `haptics.impact` tap.

```ts
export type ImpactStyle = "light" | "medium" | "heavy" | "soft" | "rigid";
```

### `NotificationFeedback`

The pattern `haptics.notification` plays.

```ts
export type NotificationFeedback = "success" | "warning" | "error";
```

### `AlertOptions`

Options for `device.ui.alert`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `string` | no | A heading above the message. |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `ConfirmOptions`

Options for `device.ui.confirm`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `destructive` | `boolean` | no | Shows the confirming button as destructive (red). |
| `okLabel` | `string` | no | The confirming button's label; "OK" by default. |

It also takes [`AlertOptions`](#alertoptions)'s properties.

### `PromptOptions`

Options for `device.ui.prompt`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placeholder` | `string` | no | Grey text shown while the field is empty. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` | no | Text the field starts with. |
| `secure` | `boolean` | no | Hides what is typed, as for a password. |

It also takes [`AlertOptions`](#alertoptions)'s properties.

### `ActionSheetOptions`

Options for `device.ui.actionSheet`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | `string` | no | A line under the title. |
| `cancel` | `string` | no | The cancel button's label; "Cancel" by default. |
| `destructive` | `number` | no | The index of an option to show as destructive (red). |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `PickDateOptions`

Options for `device.ui.pickDate`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `DateMode` | no | What to pick; "datetime" by default. |
| `title` | `string` | no | A heading above the picker. |
| `value` | `Date` | no | The date the picker starts at; now by default. |
| `min` | `Date` | no | The earliest date that can be picked. |
| `max` | `Date` | no | The latest date that can be picked. |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `DateMode`

What `device.ui.pickDate` picks.

```ts
export type DateMode = "date" | "time" | "datetime";
```

### `ShareOptions`

What `device.share` shares: at least one of `text`, `url` and `files`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | no | Text to share, such as a message or a caption. |
| `url` | `string \| URL` | no | A link to share: `http`, `https` or `mailto`. |
| `files` | `NamedBytes[]` | no | Files to share, together at most 16 MiB; their names are what the receiving app sees. |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `NamedBytes`

A file a cell hands over: a `File`, or bytes with the name to show and save them under.

```ts
export type NamedBytes = File | { name: string; data: Bytes };
```

### `Bytes`

Bytes a device method takes.

```ts
export type Bytes = Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer | Blob;
```

### `PickFilesOptions`

Options for `device.files.pick`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `types` | `string[]` | no | What may be picked: MIME types (`"text/csv"`), wildcards (`"image/*"`) or extensions (`".parquet"`). Anything by default. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | no | Whether several files may be picked; one by default. |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `ExportFileOptions`

Options for `device.files.export`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | The name the save panel suggests: a plain file name, without slashes. |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `PickPhotosOptions`

Options for `device.photos.pick`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `number` | no | How many photos may be picked; 1 by default, 0 for no limit. |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `PlaySoundOptions`

Options for `device.sound.play`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `volume` | `number` | no | From 0 to 1; 1 by default. |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `SoundState`

Where a player is: whether it is playing, and its time and length in seconds.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `playing` | `boolean` | yes | Whether it is playing now. |
| `time` | `number` | yes | Where it is, in seconds from the start. |
| `duration` | `number` | yes | The sound's length in seconds. |

### `ScheduleNotificationOptions`

Options for `device.notifications.schedule`.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delay` | `number` | yes | Seconds from now, more than 0. |
| `title` | `string` | no | Shown above the body. |

It also takes [`CallOptions`](#calloptions)'s properties.

### `PendingNotification`

A notification this notebook scheduled that hasn't been delivered.

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | What `schedule()` returned. |
| `title` | `string` | no | The title it was scheduled with. |
| `body` | `string` | yes | The text it shows. |
| `date` | `Date` | no | When it is due, when the host knows. |

### `AuthorizationStatus`

A capability's authorization. Partial grants count as granted:
`limited` (some contacts or photos), `writeOnly` (add reminders or
photos, not read them) and `reducedAccuracy` (approximate location).

```ts
export type AuthorizationStatus = "notDetermined" | "denied" | "restricted" | "authorized" | "limited" | "writeOnly" | "reducedAccuracy";
```
